answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the work and disputes resolved by slashing the stake. Splitting one operator into many accounts does not multiply voting weight unless each account locks more tokens, so a sybil attack becomes a capital-intensive bet: the attacker must buy or borrow stake, keep it locked, and risk losing it when caught. Even at the zenith of activity, a knoll of colluding agents cannot cheaply overwhelm a jetty of honest validators.
